text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Living costs: Prices of electricity and water to rise in autumn, while meat and meat products could become cheaper by some five to 13 percent.
- Construction works on the Plomin II thermal power plant to begin in September.
- Some 3,000 Croat-owned flats in Sarajevo which were abandonded during the war have been declared vacant.
- The first four tourist information machines installed in Zagreb. The machines offer basic information about Croatia and its tourist destinations in Croatian, English, German and Italian.

- Tourism Minister Niko Bulic offers his resignation after his wife won a competition for the new Croatian tourist slogan. It is up to the government to accept or reject it, but any decision is not likely before September.
- Zagreb residents' living costs down 4.7 percent in July of 1997 compared to the same month last year.
- Another apparition of the Virgin Mary rumoured to have taken place in the Adriatic town of Zadar. There has been no official reaction from the local clergy.
- Prices of cars to ease in January 1998 with the introduction of VAT at a 22 percent rate, compared to a 26.5 percent current tax levy on vehicles.
- The subpoena against Croatia will be lifted, claims Srecko Jelinic, head of the government's office for cooperation with the Hague Tribunal.

- According to June statistics, Austrian, Czech, Italian and German tourists make up the majority of foreign holidaymakers in Croatia. The number of Czech visitors rising fastest, together with Germans they accounted for more than 500,000 overnight stays in June.
- The renowned tenor Placido Domingo has a concert in Split tonight. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
